useCase.name: Close an enquiry as not interested, and re-open one closed by mistake
useCase.featureRef: 2.11 Marking a lead as declined, and re-opening it

intent.name: inquiry.close
intent.summary: Close an enquiry as not interested, with the reason the family gave. One step, and reversible by inquiry.reopen.
routesHere: close the Ahmed Raza enquiry, they went to another school

routesHere.text: ye inquiry band kar do, unhone dusre school mein admission le liya
routesHere.gloss: close this enquiry, they took admission at another school

routesHere.text: unhone mana kar diya, fees zyada thi
routesHere.gloss: they said no, the fees were too high

routesHere: mark this lead as not interested — no longer responding

routesHere.text: ye family ab interested nahi hai
routesHere.gloss: this family is not interested any more

routesHere: close it, they moved out of the city

request.text: ye inquiry ghalti se band hui thi
request.gloss: this enquiry was closed by mistake

routesElsewhere.note: The reverse of this, and it needs its own reason.

request.text: abhi soch rahe hain, baad mein call karunga
request.gloss: they are still thinking, I'll call later

routesElsewhere.note: Still considering is a contact outcome, not a closure. Closing a family who has not said no removes them from every reminder (BR-1).
A Principal's rejection is a decision on a forwarded inquiry, and it closes the enquiry itself (BR-9). Closing here is the school recording that the family withdrew.

request.text: unko bata do ke hum ne band kar diya
request.gloss: tell them we have closed it

routesElsewhere.note: Closing sends the family nothing by itself (BR-11). Telling them is a separate message, logged as one.
An enquiry is never deleted (BR-4). It moves to the Not Interested List and keeps its history, so a family who returns is recognised.

steps.note: One step. The reason is the point of the act — closing without one makes the loss report useless (BR-2).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Whether the enquiry is already closed, and whether it has been taken forward to an admission, are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write. The status change, the closure record, the contact-history entry and the audit entry are written together or not at all. Nothing is deleted — the enquiry and its full history stay readable on the Not Interested List (BR-4). Nothing is sent to the family (BR-11).

operations.name: inquiry.close
operations.idempotencyKey: inquiry_id, since an enquiry has one closure at a time and a repeat returns ALREADY_CLOSED rather than recording a second
operations.purpose: Close an enquiry as not interested, recording why, and remove it from the follow-up list and every reminder.

parameters.name: inquiry_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No enquiry matches in this branch.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with child name, guardian and status. Two families of the same name is ordinary here.

parameters.notes: The enquiry, resolved from how the actor named it — a reference, the child's name, or the guardian's number.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.type: enum: Fee too high | Chose another school | Moved away | Distance too far | No seat in the class wanted | Timing not suitable | No response after follow-up | Rejected at approval | Other
parameters.notes: Mandatory. A closure with no reason teaches the school nothing and makes the loss report useless (BR-2).

parameters.name: other_reason
parameters.notes: Required when reason is Other (BR-3, E2). Omit otherwise — sending it with a listed reason records a second explanation nobody asked for.

parameters.name: competitor_school
parameters.notes: Where the family named the school they chose. Only where the request states it; never inferred from the area.

parameters.name: closing_note
parameters.notes: Appended to the contact history, never replacing it. The family's words belong here.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The enquiry as closed, and what it kept.

fields.name: previous_status
fields.description: What it was before closing. Restored by inquiry.reopen (BR-7).

fields.name: reopenable
fields.description: False where the closure followed a rejection at approval (UC-02-11 E8).

errors.note: Message: "Select a reason before closing this enquiry." Ask which reason; do not choose one.

errors.meaning: Reason is Other with no free text.

errors.note: The message names the closure date. Not a failure to retry, and not a reason to re-open.

errors.meaning: The enquiry was taken forward to a completed admission.
errors.note: Message names the admission date. The family is a student (BR-10); there is nothing here to close.

planningRules.rule: Never close an enquiry the family has not refused. Closing removes it from every reminder (BR-1), and a family still considering who is closed is a family the school stops calling. "Soch rahe hain" and "baad mein batayenge" are contact outcomes, not closures.

Read the reason from what the family actually said, and never fall back on Other to get past a refusal. Other exists for reasons the list does not hold, and using it as a default makes the whole list stop meaning anything (BR-3). Where the sentence does not settle which reason it is, ask.
Put the family's own words in closing_note, not in reason. reason is the fixed set the loss report is built from; the words are what the next person reads when the family comes back.
Never chain a re-open onto a refusal. An enquiry already closed is an answer (E3), and re-opening to make a close succeed is nonsense — it would then be closed again with a second reason.
Never chain a message onto this plan. Closing tells the family nothing by itself (BR-11); where they are to be told, that is inquiry.message, planned separately and logged as a message.

reversal.statement: inquiry.reopen restores the enquiry to its previous status and requires a new follow-up date (BR-5, BR-7). This is the one genuinely reversible act in the module, and deliberately so: closure is a judgement made in a hurry at a desk. Re-opening is a fresh decision with its own reason, never a compensating call the controller makes on its own after a failure.

request.text: Ahmed Raza wali inquiry band kar do — unhone Beaconhouse mein admission le liya
request.gloss: close the Ahmed Raza enquiry — they took admission at Beaconhouse

steps.note: The competitor is named in the request, so it is recorded. Had the request not named one, the field would be omitted rather than guessed from the area (PR-3).

resolvedPlans.outcome: The enquiry moves to Not Interested with its full contact history intact, drops off the follow-up list, and enters the loss report under Chose another school with Beaconhouse named. Nothing is sent to the family.

request.text: unhone mana kar diya, keh rahe the fees bohat zyada hai
request.gloss: they said no, they said the fees are much too high

inputs.closing_note: Said the fees are much too high.

steps.note: "Fees bohat zyada hai" becomes the reason Fee too high, and the family's own words go to closing_note. The two are not the same field (PR-3).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Closed under Fee too high, which is the line of the loss report the school's fee decisions are read against.

resolvedPlans.request: close this one, they've stopped answering after four attempts
resolvedPlans.context: Staff, Johar Town branch, on an enquiry already flagged Stale.

steps.note: Stale and closed are different states: stale drops the enquiry out of the daily list but keeps it open (UC-02-10 BR-6). Closing it is a decision someone takes.

resolvedPlans.outcome: The enquiry closes under No response after follow-up and leaves the pipeline. It stays on the Not Interested List, so if the family returns next year they are recognised.

intent.name: inquiry.reopen
intent.summary: Re-open an enquiry closed by mistake, restoring its previous status and setting a new follow-up date. One step.
routesHere: re-open the Ahmed Raza enquiry, it was closed by mistake

routesHere.text: ye inquiry ghalti se band ho gayi thi, dobara kholo
routesHere.gloss: this enquiry was closed by mistake, open it again

routesHere.text: family ne wapas call kiya hai, inquiry khol do
routesHere.gloss: the family called back, open the enquiry

routesHere: they've changed their mind — re-open this lead and call them Monday

routesHere.text: band hui inquiry dobara chalu karni hai
routesHere.gloss: I need to restart a closed enquiry

routesElsewhere.request: open a fresh enquiry for this family
routesElsewhere.note: Where the family is enquiring about a different child, or a different academic session, that is a new enquiry rather than a re-opening.

request.text: is inquiry pe contact log kar do
request.gloss: log a contact on this enquiry

routesElsewhere.note: A closed enquiry refuses a contact log (UC-02-10 E6). Re-opening first is a separate decision, never chained.
An enquiry closed by a rejection at approval is not re-opened here (E8). A rejection is a decision, and decisions are never edited.

steps.note: One step. Both the reason and the new date are required: a lead back in the list with no date disappears again (BR-7), and a lead closed and re-opened repeatedly should be visible rather than silent (BR-6).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Whether the enquiry is closed at all, and whether it was closed by a rejection, are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write. The restored status, the re-opening record, the new follow-up date and the audit entry are written together or not at all. The closure is not erased — it stays in the history, so a re-opened enquiry never looks as though it was never closed (BR-8).

operations.name: inquiry.reopen
operations.idempotencyKey: inquiry_id + the closure it is re-opening, so a repeat does not inflate reopen_count
operations.purpose: Restore a closed enquiry to its previous status with a new follow-up date, keeping the closure in its history.

parameters.name: inquiry_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No enquiry matches in this branch.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with child name, guardian and status. Two families of the same name is ordinary here.

parameters.notes: The enquiry, resolved from how the actor named it — a reference, the child's name, or the guardian's number.

parameters.name: reopen_reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 250 characters. Mandatory, so a lead closed and re-opened repeatedly is visible rather than silent (BR-6).

parameters.name: new_follow_up_date
parameters.notes: Not in the past. Mandatory: an enquiry back in the list with no date disappears again (BR-7, E6).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: status
fields.description: The status it held before closure, restored (BR-7).

fields.name: reopen_count
fields.description: How many times this enquiry has been closed and re-opened. Visible rather than silent (BR-6).

errors.meaning: No reason was given for re-opening.
No new follow-up date was given.
errors.note: Message: "Set a follow-up date so the enquiry does not disappear again." Ask for the date; do not supply one.

errors.meaning: The follow-up date is before today.
The enquiry was closed by a rejection at approval.
errors.note: A rejection is a decision, and decisions are never edited (UC-02-07 BR-11). There is no path from here that re-opens it.
Report that it is open and at what status. UC-02-11 defines no E-id for it because the re-open control is only offered on a closed enquiry; see the open question.

planningRules.rule: Never re-open an enquiry as a step towards something else. Re-opening is a decision with a reason that someone stands behind (BR-6), and doing it silently so a contact log or a message succeeds hides that the enquiry had been closed.
Never supply new_follow_up_date yourself. E6 refuses the re-opening without one precisely so that a person commits to a date, and a date invented here re-opens a lead nobody has agreed to chase.

Never treat CLOSED_BY_REJECTION as something to route around. An enquiry closed by a Principal's rejection has a decision behind it, and decisions are never edited (UC-02-07 BR-11). There is no other capability that achieves it either.
Carry the actor's own words into reopen_reason. "Family ne wapas call kiya" is the reason; a planner's tidy paraphrase loses who did what.

reversal.statement: inquiry.close closes it again, with a fresh reason. The pair is genuinely reversible in both directions, and the history keeps every closure and every re-opening (BR-8), so the sequence survives however many times it happens. The controller must not close an enquiry on its own to undo a re-opening it made.

request.text: Ahmed Raza wali inquiry ghalti se band ho gayi thi — dobara khol do aur pir ko follow-up rakho
request.gloss: the Ahmed Raza enquiry was closed by mistake — re-open it and set the follow-up for Friday

resolvedPlans.context: Staff, Johar Town branch. Today is 07-09-2026.
resolvedPlans.outcome: The enquiry returns to Contacted, the status it held before closing, and reappears on the follow-up list for Friday. The closure stays in its history, so it does not look as though it was never closed.

request.text: wo family jo mana kar chuki thi, unhone wapas call kiya hai — inquiry khol do, kal baat karunga
request.gloss: the family who had said no called back — open the enquiry, I'll speak to them tomorrow

resolvedPlans.context: Staff, Johar Town branch. Today is 07-09-2026.

inputs.reopen_reason: Family called back and is interested again.

steps.note: The reason carries what actually happened, in the actor's own terms. reopen_count moves to 1, which is how a lead closed and re-opened repeatedly stays visible (BR-6).

resolvedPlans.outcome: The enquiry is live again with tomorrow's follow-up. Both the original closure under Fee too high and this re-opening are in the history.

resolvedPlans.request: re-open the Sana Malik enquiry, we closed it after a rejection
resolvedPlans.context: Staff, Johar Town branch, on an enquiry closed by a Principal's rejection.

steps.note: The plan is emitted unchanged — the plan does not test for the rejection beforehand. The API returns CLOSED_BY_REJECTION (E8).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is written. Report that the enquiry was closed by a rejection at approval and cannot be re-opened, and that reconsidering an admission decision is a decision the Principal takes, not a re-opening.
